title: Capacity preservation in Petri nets: a characterization at one input place and coNP-completeness at two
statement: In Petri nets with place capacities, asking whether every capacity-reachable capacity-dead marking is also dead in the uncapacitated net: the live-set characterization of CBMD-DYN-WEIGHTED-CAPACITY-001 transfers exactly to chip-firing-shaped nets (one input place per transition, distinct across transitions, no self-feedback); it remains sound but becomes incomplete if self-feedback is allowed; and it becomes unsound once a place has two consumers or a transition has two input places, as does the natural refinement that tracks which transitions can fire at all. One region of that boundary is now proved rather than censused: if every transition strictly increases the count at some place, then the net preserves the uncapacitated deadlock behaviour exactly when no transition can ever fire inside the capacity box. The witness is the all-full marking itself, so no enlargement of the capacities escapes it; the hypothesis fails precisely for transitions that drain, which is what an absorbing sink supplies and why chip-firing is not covered by it. The draining case that obstruction leaves open is itself characterized for unit-weight flow nets, where each transition takes one token from a place and either moves it to another place or discards it: preservation holds exactly when there is no set S of places such that every member has positive capacity, no drain takes from a member, every mover out of a member lands in S or in a zero-capacity place, and some mover takes from a member. The gap between those two cases is a complexity dichotomy. With at most one input place per transition the problem is decidable in polynomial time by the greatest fixpoint above; with two input places it is coNP-complete, already for unit arc weights and capacities in {0,1}, by a reduction from CNF satisfiability in which a transition is blocked exactly when its clause is satisfied. So no polynomial-time local condition is exact for multi-input transitions unless P equals NP. The polynomial side extends from unit weights to arbitrary weights, with the obstruction carrying levels rather than membership: a level function bounded by the capacities, with every drain's source below its own weight, every mover whose source reaches its weight having its destination within its production weight of capacity, and some transition's source reaching its weight. The least closure seeded at each transition in turn decides it, and is complete because it lies below every failing marking. The polynomial side is in fact about input places alone: for nets whose transitions each consume from a single place, with any number of outputs and any weights, the capacity-dead admissible markings are closed under pointwise maximum, so a greatest one exists and preservation holds exactly when that single marking is ordinarily dead. A downward fixpoint from the capacities computes it, and emits a certificate that establishes it is greatest. The termination of that procedure is compiled too: each lowering strictly drops the total token count, so from the capacities a certified greatest capacity-dead marking always exists, and preserves_decided_by_lowering states the whole single-input decision in one theorem. Between the two regimes, preservation is fixed-parameter tractable in the number of multi-input transitions: each is blocked by one of finitely many unit literals, and choosing one per such transition leaves a max-closed constraint set decided by the greatest admissible solution.
verified: Exact transfer to chip-firing-shaped nets: zero unsound and zero incomplete over 1,152 systems (2 places, 2 transitions, weights <=2, capacities <=3) and 10,368 systems (3 places, 3 transitions, weights <=1, capacities <=2), in a model coded independently of the chip-firing dossier.
Self-feedback relaxation yields 1,636 incomplete cases and zero unsound ones over the newly admitted nets, so sufficiency survives it.
Shared consumption yields 80 unsound witnesses and conjunctive input yields 48, with minimal two-place examples recorded.
The usable-transition refinement of liveness remains unsound over three boxes, with 64, 7,200 and 552 witnesses.

The all-full obstruction compiles under Lean 4.35.0 with no sorry, admit or axiom declaration: increasing_preserves_iff_inert, with observed axioms [propext, Quot.sound] and no use of Classical.choice.

The modelling step is proved rather than asserted: preserves_iff_reachable_form shows that quantifying over admissible markings and over markings capacity-reachable from admissible ones give the same property, since capacity firing stays inside the box (fire_admissible, no axioms) and every admissible marking is reachable from itself.

Census corroboration over 37,197 nets inside the class across three boxes: zero disagreements with the proved equivalence, of which 25,586 are non-inert, so the claim that all of those fail is doing work.
The increasing hypothesis is load-bearing, not decoration: outside the class the conclusion would be wrong on 39,464 nets, all of them with a draining transition.

The flow characterization compiles under Lean 4.35.0 in both directions with no proof escape: Flow.preserves_iff_no_obstruction, with observed axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] and no finiteness used.
Exact against the dossier's own semantics over 133,887 systems in four boxes: zero unsound and zero incomplete, with 54,913 preserving and 78,974 not, so neither outcome is rare.
The decision procedure is checked against the proved statement rather than assumed to match it: the greatest-fixpoint peeling and a brute-force search over all subsets of places agree in every case.

Each of the four conditions is load-bearing: dropping them produces 25,224, 24,147, 11,161 and 39,726 incomplete cases respectively, and no ablation produces unsoundness, which is the expected direction.

Membership: the complement of preservation is in NP, since an admissible marking has polynomial size even with binary capacities and both halves of 'capacity-dead and ordinarily enabled' are checked in O(PT); so preservation is in coNP.

Hardness: a reduction from CNF satisfiability in which each clause becomes one transition, taking input from its negative literals and producing into its positive ones, so that the transition is blocked exactly when the clause is satisfied; a guard construction keeps every transition fed, bounding input places between one and two.

The reduction is machine checked against this dossier's own semantics and a brute-force satisfiability oracle: 240 instances, 240 agreements, zero disagreements, with 171 satisfiable and 69 unsatisfiable, and every transition carrying between one and two input places.

The weighted obstruction compiles in both directions: WFlow.preserves_iff_no_obstruction, with observed axioms [propext, Quot.sound]; obstructionOfFailure and least_closure_is_complete depend on propext alone.

The algorithm is exact against this dossier's own semantics over 102,268 weighted systems in six boxes, with zero unsound and zero incomplete and both outcomes well populated (53,493 preserving, 48,775 not).
Both remaining steps of the algorithm are load-bearing: dropping the drain test produces 18,813 incomplete cases and dropping the capacity test 33,801.

Completeness of the decision procedure is compiled, not assumed: Forced is an inductive predicate recording the lower bounds any failing marking must satisfy, forced_le_of_bad proves a forced level really is such a lower bound, and justified_closure_is_complete needs only that each level of the closure is zero or forced.

That hypothesis is machine-checked against the procedure rather than asserted to match it: over the same boxes, all 48,775 accepted closures carry a derivation satisfying the inductive rules and none fails to.
Closure under pointwise maximum compiles (SNet.capDead_max, axioms [propext, Quot.sound]) and is where the single-input hypothesis is spent; it uses no finiteness.

Preservation reduces to one marking: SNet.preserves_iff_greatest_ordDead depends on no axioms, and SNet.preserves_iff_capped_ordDead discharges the greatest-marking hypothesis from a certificate via SNet.capped_ge_of_bad.
The algorithm is exact over 31,905 single-input systems with arbitrary outputs and weights, zero unsound and zero incomplete, with 16,205 preserving and 15,700 not.

Every accepted run's certificate is re-derived from the capacities by a separate checker, which accepts a lowering step only when the transition would really be capacity-enabled at the vector reached so far: 31,905 replayed, none failed.
Both steps of the algorithm are load-bearing: dropping the overflow test gives 15,700 wrong verdicts and stopping after a single pass gives 784.

Termination is compiled, not asserted: sumBelow_lt (no axioms) gives strict decrease of a sum from a pointwise bound plus one strict drop, total_lt transports it to markings, and exists_capped_capDead runs the induction on an explicit bound to produce a certified greatest capacity-dead marking from the capacities.
preserves_decided_by_lowering states the single-input case end to end: there is a marking reached from the capacities by lowering such that preservation holds exactly when it is ordinarily dead.

Compiling the termination exposed a hypothesis that had been implicit: each transition must actually consume from the place named as its input. The SNet structure only required pre to vanish off that place.

The reduction is also checked exhaustively rather than only by sampling: over every CNF on two variables with at most three clauses of width at most two, 164 formulas, 138 satisfiable and 26 not, with zero disagreements and every transition carrying one or two input places.

The fixed-parameter procedure is exact over 145,953 general nets, 114,048 of them with a multi-input transition, with zero unsound and zero incomplete; dropping upper-bound literals gives 20,848 wrong verdicts and dropping lower-bound literals 8,074.

Its core is compiled: notCapEnabled_max_of_single gives max-closure per single-input transition, ub_max and lb_max give it for unit bounds, the two blocking lemmas give soundness of each literal, and blocked_by_some_literal gives exhaustiveness of the branching.

The hardness reduction is compiled (revision 0.9.0): preserves_iff_unsatisfiable proves that the net built from the guarded form of any CNF preserves exactly when the CNF is unsatisfiable, and guard_neg_count with probe_input_places and clause_input_places gives one or two input places per transition. A bridge check over 404 formulas confirms the compiled net equals the census's net, and detects a deliberately wrong transcription in 375 of them.
unresolved: a formal proof of the complexity-class statement: the reduction's correctness and input-place bounds are compiled (revision 0.9.0), while membership in coNP and the reduction's polynomial running time remain written arguments
direct comparison of the revision 0.4.0 reduction against the 3-SAT reduction of Yamauchi and Watanabe 1999, whose full text was not obtained
whether the queueing-with-blocking line (Liebeherr and Akyildiz; Kundu and Akyildiz) also covers the non-conservative case; the papers located are framed around closed networks

a closed-form structural characterization for multi-input nets; none can be polynomial unless P = NP (revision 0.4.0), and the fixed-parameter procedure of revision 0.8.0 decides them without characterizing them
nonclaims: finite censuses over stated boxes; no unbounded theorem about general Petri nets
the chip-firing characterization itself is proved elsewhere; this dossier only maps its reach
not a novelty determination
the all-full obstruction is proved only for nets in which every transition strictly increases some place; chip-firing with an absorbing sink is outside it, which is the point
the census in verification/allfull.py corroborates the Lean theorem and is not the proof
the flow characterization covers unit arc weights only; nothing here covers weighted flow or multi-input transitions
the greatest fixpoint is how the condition is decided on a finite net; the proved statement is the existential one, and their agreement is checked rather than assumed
the coNP-completeness statement is a written argument, not a compiled theorem; formalizing it needs a model of computation that is out of scope for this dossier
the impossibility of a polynomial-time local condition for multi-input transitions is conditional on P not equal to NP
the obstruction is a trap in the original net and a siphon in the complemented one; both are standard objects, and no novelty is claimed for the condition itself

the coNP-completeness here is not comparable to the PSPACE-completeness of deadlock for 1-safe nets (Cheng, Esparza and Palsberg 1995): that problem quantifies over reachable markings and this one does not
the clause-to-transition reduction is a standard template; encoding SAT into siphon-shaped conditions is established practice
the monotone closure is the classical maximal-trap fixpoint, known to be polynomial; only its level-valued generalization was not located
revision 0.6.0 supersedes the decision procedure of revision 0.5.0, not its characterization; the level obstruction remains the statement of what a failure looks like
single input place per transition; outputs and arc weights are unconstrained, and nothing here covers two input places

for unit-weight single-output conservative nets the obstruction is known as a cycle of full buffers, with an exact deadlock-freedom iff in the queueing-with-blocking literature; revision 0.3.0 is a restatement in a setting that additionally has drains and zero capacities
the absence of reachability in this dossier's question is the degenerate case of that literature's job-count condition, not an independent vantage point
on the proved side nothing is left in prose for the single-input case; what remains prose in this dossier is the complexity statement of revision 0.4.0
the exhaustive pass covers a small box and the random pass larger instances; neither proves the reduction, which is the written argument
the fixed-parameter procedure is the classical branching on a strong backdoor to Horn (Nishimura, Ragde and Szeider) applied with threshold literals; no new technique is claimed

the clause-level reduction preserves_iff_no_nonzero_model needs NoTautology (no atom with both signs in one clause) and is false without it; the end-to-end theorem discharges it for the guarded encoding
smallest_decisive_test: Exhibit a chip-firing-shaped net satisfying the conditions with a capacity-dead, ordinarily enabled marking; or a polynomial-time algorithm deciding preservation for nets with two input places per transition, which would collapse coNP to P; or an error in the reduction, exhibited as a CNF whose constructed net's preservation verdict differs from its unsatisfiability.
